tier_reason: Independent public harness aras-p/bcn_decoder_tester (src/main.cpp: 20 runs per DDS file, convection submodule pinned at 350416d, output-hash check that only warns) with Windows flags in CMakePresets.json (x64-release and x64-release-clang = RelWithDebInfo) plus /Ob2 in CMakeLists.txt, compilers VS2022 and clang 14 named in the chart titles, CPU Ryzen 5950X; all three chart PNGs show convection as the top BC6Hu bar. The measured convection commit is dated the same day as the repo's last commit (a BC6H bit-framing fix), so there is no later-fixed-code cap; the macOS chart lacks flags but the Windows charts alone meet A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: BC6H unsigned decode, Mpix/s, single thread, printed bar labels in aras-p's three chart PNGs (ratios derived from page data): Ryzen 5950X VS2022: convection 101 vs bcdec 85 (1.19x), swiftshader 70, mesa 57, DirectXTex 25 (4.0x), amd_cmp 9 (11x). Ryzen 5950X clang14: convection 105 vs bcdec 104 (1.01x, a tie), swiftshader 97, mesa 79, DirectXTex 34 (3.1x), amd_cmp 33 (3.2x). Apple M1 Max clang13: convection 149 vs swiftshader 143 (1.04x), mesa 84, bcdec 79 (1.89x), DirectXTex 37 (4.0x), amd_cmp 30 (5.0x). The post's own words: 'Fastest BC6H decoder (by a small margin)'. On BC7 decode it is slower than bcdec and far slower than bc7enc_rdo's bc7decomp (VS2022: convection 124 vs bcdec 142 vs bc7dec_rdo 621; clang14: 121 vs 169 vs 656; M1 Max: 157 vs 220 vs 517).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Windows: Visual Studio 2022 (cl, preset x64-release) and clang 14 (clang-cl, preset x64-release-clang), both CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE RelWithDebInfo plus /Ob2 from CMakeLists.txt, C++17; macOS: Apple clang 13, no preset or build type given. Versions per the post: convection 350416d (2022-06-23), bcdec e3ca0 (2022-06-23), DirectXTex 679538e, compressonator b2b4ee3, swiftshader 2b79b2f, mesa ad3d6d9.
corrections.caveats: Decoder only: the README makes only an unquantified claim ('very high quality at good speed') and labels its BC6H support 'Experimental'; no encode comparison against ispc_texcomp, bc7enc or Compressonator was found. The BC6H margin is small (1.19x over bcdec with VS2022, a 1% tie with clang 14, 1.04x over SwiftShader on M1 Max) and the post itself says 'by a small margin'. The bcdec measured was e3ca0 (2022-06-23, right after aras-p's speedup PR #1); the harness later moved its bcdec submodule to 026acf9 (2022-09-15) without new charts, so current bcdec may close the gap and a re-run is needed. The harness calls the internal per-block API cvtt::Internal::BC6HComputer::UnpackOne rather than the public cvtt::Kernels::DecodeBC6HU, and converts each half to float with its own half_to_float_fast5 inside the timed loop, so all BC6H decoders are timed to the same float32 RGB output (bcdec through bcdec_bc6h_float). Output hashes are checked against _hashes.txt but a mismatch only prints a warning. Windows flags come from the public CMake presets; macOS flags are not stated. The post text was read from raw.githubusercontent.com/aras-p/aras-p.hugo (content/blog/2022/06-bcn-decode-libraries.md) because aras-p.info is blocked here; the figures are the printed bar labels of static/img/blog/2022/bcn-decode-win-vs2022.png, bcn-decode-win-clang14.png and bcn-decode-mac.png. The measured commit (2022-06-23, 350416d per the harness README) is dated the same day as the repo's last commit, 'Fix bit framing error in BC6H decoder'; nothing has been committed since, so the project is abandoned.

notes: Numbers verified verbatim against all three chart PNGs and the post source; tier A stands on the Windows charts (public harness, pinned submodules, RelWithDebInfo plus /Ob2, Ryzen 5950X), consistent with retier-32's reading of the same post for bcdec. baseline_in_list set to false because bcdec and DirectXTex are not among the image-codecs baselines (libjpeg-turbo, libpng, libwebp, libavif). Shortcomings to record: tiny BC6H margin (tie with bcdec on clang 14), slower than bcdec and bc7enc_rdo on BC7, BC6H marked Experimental, internal API timed, harness hash check warns only, macOS flags unstated, abandoned since 2022-06-23.

tier_reason: Independent third-party measurement (atomic14, not the JPEGDEC author) with public code at atomic14/esp32-jpeg-perf-tests (src/main.cpp times each library's decode with millis(); src/JPEGDECTest.cpp, TJPEGTest.cpp, JPEGDecoderTest.cpp) and -Ofast in platformio.ini on an ESP32-S3. Not A: toolchain version (platform = espressif32 unpinned), library versions and clock are not stated, and it is one image with one timed decode per library.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Decode-only ms from atomic14's README table (one 280x240 JPEG, ESP32-S3): Bodmer/JPEGDecoder (picojpeg) 108, Bodmer/TJpg_Decoder (TJpgDec) 55, bitbank2/JPEGDEC 32 (2023 run, struck through), JPEGDEC 'New!' SIMD version 23 (added 2024-04-07; other rows not re-run), ESP32_JPEG 20. Derived from page data: JPEGDEC is 1.7x faster than TJpgDec in the same session (55/32) and 2.4x with the 2024 number (55/23, cross-session); 3.4x and 4.7x faster than picojpeg (108/32, 108/23). Espressif's ESP32_JPEG is faster still (20 ms). Decode plus draw: TJpg_Decoder 64, JPEGDEC 38 (old) or 29 (new), ESP32_JPEG 37 (JPEGDecoder's 118 is hard-coded as decode + 10 in main.cpp). The JPEGDEC README chart (perf.jpg) gives only its own per-MCU timings (tulips.h 640x480: ESP32-S3 @240MHz 91,516 us full decode, Cortex-M7 @600MHz 29,592 us, Apple M1 8,014 us full and 992 us at 1/8 size) and unquantified claims ('perform better than anything else available', 'cropping function that's faster than JPEGTRAN').
corrections.compiler_and_flags: PlatformIO platform espressif32 (unpinned), Arduino framework, build_flags -Ofast (applied to project and library sources); GCC version and library versions (bitbank2/JPEGDEC, bodmer/JPEGDecoder, Bodmer/TJpg_Decoder and ESP32_JPEG from git HEAD) not pinned.
corrections.hardware: ESP32-S3 with PSRAM (README); the 2023 rows match the initial esp32-s3-devkitc-1 env with -DBOARD_HAS_PSRAM; the 2024 'New!' JPEGDEC row was added when that env had PSRAM commented out and a um_tinys3 (TinyS3) env existed, so its board is not stated; clock speed not stated.
corrections.caveats: Evidence is an independent but small demo: one 280x240 image, one timed decode per library per loop pass (millis() resolution, no repeats or statistics), toolchain and library versions unpinned, clock not stated. Harness asymmetries: TJpgDec's output callback memcpys every block into a DMA buffer even in the decode-only pass while JPEGDEC's callback returns at once when no TFT is passed (a small bias toward JPEGDEC); main.cpp hard-codes the first library's (Bodmer/JPEGDecoder) decode+draw time as decode + 10 ms, so that column is not measured (the decode-only column behind the claims is measured). The 23 ms 'New!' row was added in 2024 without re-running the other libraries, at a time when the devkitc env had PSRAM disabled (which compiles out the ESP32_JPEG test), so it may come from a different board or config than the 2023 rows. Espressif's ESP32_JPEG was faster in decode-only (20 vs 23 ms). No published comparison against desktop libjpeg-turbo or stb_image was found, and the lead's '1/8-scale progressive in about 18 KB' claim has no numbers. The README chart (perf.jpg) shows only JPEGDEC across boards. Espressif's esp_jpeg README speed table (GitHub copy) covers TJpgDec configurations on a different image only, not JPEGDEC; an esp32.com thread comparing ROM tjpgd and JPEGDEC is blocked here (snippet only).

notes: Table numbers verified verbatim in atomic14's README and the harness code read; metadata matches (Apache-2.0, 631 stars, 75 forks, 212 commits, last commit 2026-03-13 'Fixed 2 issues which occur when decoding progressive images', active). baseline_in_list set to false: TJpgDec and picojpeg are widely used MCU decoders but not among the image-codecs baselines. Shortcomings to record: one-image single-run demo, unpinned versions, hard-coded decode+draw value for JPEGDecoder, callback copy asymmetry, cross-session 2024 row, ESP32_JPEG faster.

tier_reason: First-party README table against FFmpeg 8.1.2 (libwebp encoder at default m4, native VP8/VP8L decoder) with a described method (pinned single core, ABBA pairs, null-arm floor) but no WebP harness script, corpus, CPU, rustc version or flags published; the only bench code, examples/decode_bench.rs, times rusty_webp alone.

corrections.stars_or_usage: remade_ffmpeg_rs 6 stars, 0 forks, 506 commits; crates.io rusty_webp 0.1.1 (1,025 downloads; 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 both published 2026-08-12)
corrections.caveats: First-party, and the WebP harness is not in the repo: tools/bench has the generic ABBA harness pinab.py (pins one CPU and parses the arm's printed duration; its usage text is audio-shaped) and codec-bench.ps1 but no WebP script, docs/benchmarks.md covers VP9 only (Intel Core i7-14650HX), crates/rusty_webp/examples holds only decode_bench.rs (times rusty_webp alone, under the project's custom global allocator rusty_alloc_api::RustyAlloc), and the Derf corpus is not shipped; compiler, flags and CPU for the WebP rows are unstated. The README says 'child CPU time', which for the ffmpeg CLI arm includes demux and any pixel-format conversion against an in-process Rust arm; the companion remade_ffmpeg_rs record found that pattern inflated its MP3 margin. The libwebp baseline is reached through FFmpeg's libwebp wrapper, not cwebp, and only at m4: there is no speed comparison against libwebp's faster efforts m0-m3, although on photos the encoder lands between m0 and m4 in size (+4-13% over m4). Decode wins are against FFmpeg's native VP8/VP8L decoder, not libwebp's dwebp; upstream image-webp's README says its decode runs at 70-100% of libwebp's speed. NOTICE.md records that upstream image-webp v0.2.4's encoder (the fork's starting point, not a first version of the fork) was 16-23x faster than libwebp but produced 35-53% larger files on photos (+656% on repeated-content screen material), so the 1.6-2.8x is a deliberate size/speed trade and the fork's encoder is much slower than the upstream one it replaced. Repository shows AI assistance (CLAUDE.md, .claude directory, commits co-authored by claude); the rusty_webp path has two commits, both 2026-08-12 (repo-wide last commit 2026-10-05). The repo LICENSE is Apache-2.0; the crate is MIT OR Apache-2.0 with the upstream license files kept. Shares repo_url with the remade_ffmpeg_rs record (video-audio), hence the paper:rusty-webp id.

notes: README numbers verified verbatim (lossy 8K decode 1.24-1.29x bit-exact, lossless 8K decode ~2.15x, lossless encode 1.6-2.8x faster than libwebp m4 at +4-13% size on photos, up to 39% smaller on screen content); metadata matches. Corrected the NOTICE reading: the 16-23x / 35-53% figures describe upstream image-webp's encoder, not an earlier rusty_webp. Not a duplicate: the existing remade_ffmpeg_rs record covers the audio codecs. Shortcomings to record: harness and corpus unpublished, CPU and flags unstated, CLI child-time against in-process arm, custom allocator, decode baseline is FFmpeg not libwebp, encode compared only at m4.
